summary: Iteration 38 verified. BACKEND (4/4 pytest): (a) POST a large PNG item then GET /api/items — list `photo` was 3752 chars vs stored 59996 chars (~94% smaller), NO `orig_photo` on list items, NO `thumb` leaked as separate field, and GET /api/items/{id} returned the full photo (15640 chars > 3752 list char). Total /api/items payload for the reviewer wardrobe with 1 test item was only 4222 bytes — tiny. (b) Dress Me: explicit occasion returned resolved_items each with a valid necessity in {core|recommended|optional}, core was a real outfit (Top + Bottom + Shoes), and NO backpack/briefcase/laptop/work bag was styled. Relaxed occasion ('relaxing at home') returned a top+bottom+shoes look with NO bag and NO jewellery (reported, not required). FRONTEND: reviewer login OK, 15 taxonomy fixtures seeded and cleaned up. Bottoms subs = [Trousers·2, Lounge Pants·3] in the correct order (empty ones hidden); Navy drawstring / Pink / Black track pants under Lounge Pants; Black tailored trousers + Navy chinos under Trousers. Shoes subs = [Heels, Flats] — Sandals chip GONE; Tan wedge sandals + Black heeled sandals under Heels; Brown flat sandals + Black slides under Flats. Bags subs = [Handbags, Clutches] only; Small crossbody bag + Black leather backpack under Handbags; Gold evening clutch under Clutches. Olive long sleeve top stays under Tops>Long Sleeve while Grey sweatshirt + Black hoodie both classify to Outerwear>Jumpers. No 'Other' chip anywhere; each item resolves to exactly one chip. Dress Me: CORE group renders unlabelled, RECOMMENDED heading + group visible; OPTIONAL group hidden because the AI returned no optional items (per the design — headings only render when items exist). Single-item swap picker still opens on tapping a piece. Regression smoke: item detail image renders full-size, /add-item shows CATEGORY chips, /bulk-add opens, Shopping Intelligence entry present on wardrobe, Home has 'Plan Your Week' section (below the fold), Premium page has 'Occasion planning' and NO 'Capsule wardrobes'. ONE PERFORMANCE MISS: opening an item and pressing back fired an extra GET /api/items within the 60s freshness window (delta=1), instead of 0. The category+subfilter WAS preserved and no loading flash was seen, but the wardrobe cache is being invalidated (or the focus effect races the initial cache write) on the first back-nav — see rca_of_issue.

integration_issues.issue: Opening an item and pressing back within 60s fired 1 extra GET /api/items (delta=1) despite wardrobeIsFresh() being intended to suppress it. Category, subfilter and item list ARE preserved and no loading spinner flashed, but the network call happens. Suspect wardrobeIsFresh() is returning false on the first focus-back either because the initial `load()` had not yet run setCachedItems() before the user tapped a card, or something in the item-detail navigation is marking the cache dirty. Also observed 3 GET /api/items calls on initial wardrobe entry — worth a look. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/wardrobe.tsx:58-75 & /app/frontend/src/utils/wardrobeCache.ts.

action_items: Investigate the extra GET /api/items on back-nav within the 60s cache window (delta=1). Most likely fixes: (i) in useFocusEffect, check wardrobeIsFresh() BEFORE the setItems(cache) line and gate the `load()` behind a `mounted && !wardrobeIsFresh()` guard; (ii) ensure item-detail/log-wear paths only call markWardrobeDirty() when they actually mutate; (iii) verify that the 3 initial GET /api/items on wardrobe entry (before any user action) collapse to 1 — the profile context may be re-firing the focus effect. Not a launch blocker but is the main perf win users will feel.
Optional: reduce the 3 initial GET /api/items to 1 on wardrobe entry — currently the profileLoading transition + focus effect + mount all race and produce multiple fetches.
critical_code_review_comments: taxonomy.ts is Hermes-safe: no lookbehinds, only forward regexes with \b word boundaries and explicit ordering. Bottoms SUB_RULES puts Lounge Pants BEFORE Jeans/Trousers so 'lounge/track/drawstring/jogger/sweat/pyjama/harem/elastic waist/pull-on' catch first; Trousers is the tailored/chino/palazzo/cargo/wide-leg/suit-pant catch. Shoes puts Heels (heel|wedge|platform sandal) after Sneakers/Boots and Flats (which includes sandal|slide|thong|flip-flop|ballet|loafer) last — so heeled sandals correctly land in Heels and flat sandals in Flats. Bags collapses to Handbags + Clutches only, and the Handbags regex explicitly captures backpack|rucksack|briefcase|laptop bag|work bag so they migrate correctly.

Outerwear Jumpers regex now requires warmth-layer construction (sweatshirt|hoodie|hooded|fleece|pullover|cable knit|chunky knit|knitted jumper|crewneck sweat) — a lightweight long-sleeve top no longer falls into Jumpers. Verified with Olive long-sleeve top vs Grey sweatshirt / Black hoodie split.

server.py make_thumb() uses PIL Image.thumbnail() at 320px; GET /api/items excludes orig_photo, substitutes thumb into photo, pops thumb from output, and does a bounded lazy backfill (max 20 legacy items per call). Detail endpoint still returns full photo. Behaviour matched observed byte counts.

STYLIST_SYSTEM prompt explicitly demands core|recommended|optional necessity and forbids backpack/briefcase/laptop/work bag as the outfit bag. _build_outfit() normalises invalid necessity values to 'core' — good defensive default.

dressme.tsx renders necessity groups only when rows exist (line 315: `if (!rows.length) return null;`) — matches the tested outcome (OPTIONAL group not rendered when AI returned no optional items). The core group heading is intentionally the empty string.

wardrobe.tsx useFocusEffect logic in lines 58-75 sets items from cache first, then checks wardrobeIsFresh() — but if the cache exists yet is not fresh, `load()` still fires. That's correct in isolation but the observed delta=1 on back-nav suggests either wardrobeIsFresh() legitimately returned false (fetchedAt=0 or dirty=true) or the effect fires multiple times because profileLoading transitioned. Worth an explicit trace.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% — taxonomy 15/15 items in correct chips, Dress Me grouping renders correctly, single-item swap works, regression smoke clean; ONE finding: back-nav triggered 1 extra GET /api/items within the 60s freshness window

seed_data_creation: Seeded 15 reviewer items via API (all names prefixed 'TEST_iter38') for taxonomy verification. ALL 15 deleted after testing (verified {"deleted": 15}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter38 backend (thumbnails + Dress Me necessity) is solid — pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration38_thumbs_necessity.py is a reusable regression pack (uses PIL to generate a real large PNG payload). Frontend taxonomy 100%: Bottoms/Shoes/Bags simplification and Long Sleeve vs Jumper split all classify correctly. Dress Me groups render only when populated (matches spec). ONE outstanding perf finding: back-nav from item detail fires 1 extra GET /api/items within the 60s freshness window; also 3 initial GETs on wardrobe entry. Neither breaks UX (no spinner flash, filter/sub preserved) but the cache miss on back-nav defeats part of the intended performance win — the main agent should trace why wardrobeIsFresh() returns false at that moment (setCachedItems race with the profile-context focus effect is the leading hypothesis).
rca_of_issue: Extra GET /api/items on back-nav: The wardrobe uses `useFocusEffect(() => { const cache = getCachedItems(); if (cache && cache !== items) setItems(cache); if (wardrobeIsFresh()) return; if (!profileLoading) load(...); })`. wardrobeIsFresh() requires `cached != null && !dirty && Date.now()-fetchedAt < 60_000`. On first back-nav from item detail, delta=1 GET was observed. Two hypotheses: (a) profileLoading transitions during item-detail unmount/remount, retriggering the effect BEFORE the previous load() has populated the cache — the effect runs again, sees fetchedAt=0, and re-fetches; (b) something in the item-detail flow (perhaps deleting or wearing an item) is calling markWardrobeDirty() unconditionally. Repro: login as reviewer, wardrobe → Bottoms → Lounge Pants → tap a card → item-back → observe network shows GET /api/items. Suggested mitigation: gate `load()` in useFocusEffect with an explicit `if (getCachedItems() && !dirty && Date.now()-fetchedAt<60_000) return` inline, OR early-return when `restored.current` was just flipped from a back-nav.
